title: Impact of previous acute and chronic stress on negative glucocorticoid feedback in laboratory animal: Theoretical background and methodological concerns
title_zh: 先前急性与慢性压力对实验动物负面糖皮质激素反馈的影响：理论背景与方法学关注
abstract: Chronic stress or acute severe stressors have been extensively used as putative animal models of psychiatric diseases, particularly depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), respectively. The hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis not only represents a prototypical stress response system, but also mediates or modulates a wide range of the behavioral and physiological consequences of stress exposure. Therefore, particular attention has been paid to the parallelisms between stress-induced alterations of the HPA axis in animal models and the alterations observed in PTSD and depression. The canonical views suggest that PTSD patients are characterized by hypocortisolemia and an enhanced negative glucocorticoid feedback (nGF), whereas major depression patients typically show hypercortisolemia and impaired nGF. Here, we critically review studies on the effects of different stress models on nGF, distinguishing between nGF under resting and stress conditions. The evidence that chronic stress exposure is associated with impaired nGF is weak, except for HPA activity under resting conditions. The evidence that a single exposure to severe stressors leads to enhanced nGF under stress conditions is controversial, and the studies supporting this present important limitations. In general, the major limitations of nGF studies are the lack of plasma ACTH data, the assessment of nGF using exposure to a stressor with which animals have prior experience, and the predominant use of dexamethasone instead of natural glucocorticoids. At the dexamethasone doses typically used, this drug acts mainly at the anterior pituitary rather than at the brain level, making it difficult to relate altered nGF with changes in brain corticosteroid receptors.
abstract_zh: 慢性压力或急性严重压力源已被广泛用作精神疾病的动物模型，尤其是抑郁症和创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。下丘脑-垂体-肾上腺（HPA）轴不仅是典型的压力反应系统，还介导或调节压力暴露所产生的广泛行为和生理后果。因此，研究者特别关注动物模型中压力诱导的HPA轴改变与PTSD及抑郁症中观察到的改变之间的相似性。传统观点认为，PTSD 患者表现为皮质醇低下和增强的负面糖皮质激素反馈（nGF），而重度抑郁患者则通常呈现皮质醇升高和 nGF 受损。本文对不同压力模型对 nGF 的影响进行批判性综述，区分静息状态与压力状态下的 nGF。除静息状态下 HPA 活动外，慢性压力暴露与 nGF 损害相关的证据较弱。单次严重压力暴露导致压力状态下 nGF 增强的证据存在争议，且支持此结论的研究存在重要局限。总体而言，nGF 研究的主要局限包括缺乏血浆 ACTH 数据、使用动物已有经验的压力源评估 nGF，以及主要使用地塞米松而非天然糖皮质激素。地塞米松在常用剂量下主要作用于前叶垂体而非脑部，使得将 nGF 变化与脑内皮质激素受体变化关联变得困难。
